answer: A harbour registry can resist sybils by requiring every new agent to lock a refundable bond before it may trade: the agent must stake scarce compute time and complete one verified delivery at the wharf, with its timber shipments and service record published as a public plume of evidence. Spinning up thousands of fake identities then costs real bonded capital and weeks of auditable work each, while one honest agent pays once and reuses its reputation, so forgery scales linearly in cost but honest participation does not.
